div.head: PREFACE SCIENCE is very good in its own way, but we observe a wide-spread and lamentable ignorance concerning all that pertains to the romantic side of our earth’s history. It is to dispel this ignorance that the following facts are made public.
div.p: SCIENCE is very good in its own way, but we observe a wide-spread and lamentable ignorance concerning all that pertains to the romantic side of our earth’s history. It is to dispel this ignorance that the following facts are made public.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
I.
div.p: One summer’s night, about a million years ago, it happened that the Moon was pensive.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
II.
div.p: It also happened that the Earth was floating leisurely about in space as if he thought himself a thing of beauty. But she affected not to see him.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
III.
div.p: Old Saturn did, however, and understood it all. For æons he had loved this Moon, but she had chilled him to the marrow whenever he approached.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
IV.
div.p: When he saw the Earth go nearer and nearer, and finally sit beside her, and even then get nearer still and tell her something in an earnest manner, and she enjoy it all, his spirit boiled within him.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
V.
div.p: He swore to spoil the fun, then burst upon them in a fury.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
VI.
div.p: They had an ugly fight, tearing about the Heavens for hours, bumping into other Planets, and deranging the whole solar system.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
VII.
div.p: But the Earth was a lusty boy, and finally got in a scorching blow between the old beau’s eyes that sent him whirling into space.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
VIII.
div.p: And never since has he annoyed the Moon.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
IX.
div.p: While this was going on, the Sun, also a lover of the Moon, had risen with the dawn, as usual, and prepared for his morning drive.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
X.
div.p: As he approached the scene of all this trouble he took in the situation at a glance, and at once made a formal offer of marriage.
But she declined respectfully, saying she was already promised to the Earth.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
XI.
div.p: But Sol was hot-headed, and not accustomed to defeat.
He carried her off by main force, and said, “If ever I see you and the Earth together, I will burn you both to a cinder!”

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
XII.
div.p: So it is only while the Sun is sleeping that she can see her lover.

div.head:
[Image unavailable.]
XIII.
div.p: She hovers over him at night, and her tears that fall upon the Earth are what we call the dew.
